usual_baseline: Usually well under the 20% benchmark in UK units: 3.05–14.3%, with 4.67% and 5% typical. One cohort was 29%, and 43.5% in women of child-bearing age [2156]. Rates are higher in women (18.1% vs 11.1%) and those aged 16–25 (11.54%).
fix_that_works: More preoperative cross-sectional imaging, 69% to 88%, went with a fall from 10.3% to 3% [2690].
fix_that_fails: An undescribed action plan left the overall rate at 25% and 37% in women of child-bearing age [2156]. One trust drifted from 2.04% to 4.67% despite universal imaging (not significant) [2872].
consultant_advice: Most units now sit far below 20%, so a simple rate audit rarely shows a problem. If you must, study young women and imaging-negative versus imaging-positive cases, or the other side: missed appendicitis and perforation from avoiding surgery, which none of these measured.
